docRequirement: `agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts.md:54` (re-fetched 2026-08-02, 477 lines): "The SDK reads CLAUDE.md when the matching setting source is enabled: `'project'` loads `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md` from the working directory, and `'user'` loads `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`." The same line adds "Default `query()` options enable both sources" and ":112" adds "It is not loaded if you pass an empty `settingSources` array"; `:360` restates the `project`-source gate. `:48`/`:52` bind WHERE it goes: the content is injected "into the conversation as project context, not into the system prompt". This is not SDK-only — `memory.md:60`'s load table gives **Project instructions** as "`./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md`" and `memory.md:69` repeats "A project CLAUDE.md can be stored in either `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md`". Note the scope of the alternative location: `memory.md:63` and `:153` spell the ancestor walk with the bare names only ("checking each directory along the way for `CLAUDE.md` and `CLAUDE.local.md`"), and `:157` spells the subdirectory walk the same way, so `.claude/CLAUDE.md` is bound at the working directory / project root, not at every ancestor level.
current: The eager project-instruction candidate list is `PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES = ['AGENTS.md', 'CLAUDE.md', 'CLAUDE.local.md']` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:82), and every consumer joins a BARE NAME onto a directory: the working-directory tier `join(workingDirectory, name)` (native-sources.ts:1088-1091), the ancestor walk `join(dir, name)` (native-sources.ts:1074-1087), the workspace-root tier `join(context.workspaceRootPath, name)` (native-sources.ts:987-990), the nested on-demand walk `join(dir, fileName)` (native-sources.ts:845-853), and the pre-trust consent detector `join(root, name)` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts:134-137). `.claude` IS read in the same function for three other things — `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json` as permission records via `join(workingDirectory, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, name)` (native-sources.ts:1051-1059) and `.claude/rules` as a memory tier via `CLAUDE_RULES_DIR` (native-sources.ts:727, used at :971 and :1108-1114) — but nothing ever joins `.claude` to `CLAUDE.md`. `grep -ran '\.claude/CLAUDE\.md' packages apps docs` finds five `.ts` hits and all five are prose comments (capabilities/types.ts:199, agent/base-agent.ts:980, agent/memory/memory-store.ts:205, and two test headers). One incidental leak exists: `discoverNestedInstructionFiles` (native-sources.ts:818-856) treats `.claude` as an ordinary subdirectory, so once the agent reads any file under `<cwd>/.claude/`, the probe at base-agent.ts:1206-1219 -> `activateNestedInstructionFiles` (base-agent.ts:1230-1264) delivers `<cwd>/.claude/CLAUDE.md` into the MESSAGE HISTORY (capped at `MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILES = 8` / `MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILE_BYTES = 10 KiB`, native-sources.ts:764/772) rather than the pinned block, and `memory.md:447` semantics mean it is not re-injected after a compaction (base-agent.ts:1637-1644). The legacy fallback route is the same shape and also misses it: `CONTEXT_FILE_PATTERNS = ['agents.md', 'claude.md', 'claude.local.md']` (packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:32) is directory-level. On the Claude backend the SDK does its own discovery — `settingSources: ['user', 'project', 'local']` (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:305, comment at :302-304 explicitly names CLAUDE.md discovery) — so that one backend gets the file via the SDK while our own inventory still does not.
divergence: One of the two documented locations for the project instruction file is missing from every EAGER discovery path. Nothing about the existing behaviour is wrong — `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md` and `AGENTS.md` at the directory root load correctly, in the documented root-down order, into the pinned block; the candidate list is simply one entry short at the working-directory tier. It is not a key-name error and not a value error: it is a missing path candidate, `join(workingDirectory, '.claude', 'CLAUDE.md')`. Scope of the delta, precisely: (a) `<cwd>/.claude/CLAUDE.md` never enters the pinned instruction block at launch and reaches context only incidentally, if and when some file under `<cwd>/.claude/` is read in the same capability generation; (b) an ANCESTOR's `.claude/CLAUDE.md` is never loaded at all — but that matches `memory.md:153`, so it is NOT part of this divergence and must not be 'fixed' by adding the joined path to the ancestor walk; (c) adjacent and latent, on the same doc sentence: `projectSourceEnabled` (native-sources.ts:893-894) gates only the RULE tiers (:1035, :1100) and not the instruction pushes (:987, :1079-1091), so an explicit `settingSources` that omits `project` would still load project CLAUDE.md — latent today because no production caller sets `context.settingSources` (`grep -ran settingSources packages apps` outside tests hits only native-sources.ts:893-894, types.ts:195 and the Claude SDK options at claude-agent.ts:305).

change.what: Add a second, path-bearing candidate list and use it ONLY at the working-directory tier. Declare it AFTER `CLAUDE_RULES_DIR` (:726-727) — it cannot extend `PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES` at :82 because `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is declared 644 lines later (TDZ at module eval) and because the other four consumers must not change: `export const WORKING_DIRECTORY_INSTRUCTION_FILES: ReadonlyArray<{ relativePath: string; logicalName: string }> = [{ relativePath: 'AGENTS.md', logicalName: 'AGENTS.md' }, { relativePath: 'CLAUDE.md', logicalName: 'CLAUDE.md' }, { relativePath: join(CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, 'CLAUDE.md'), logicalName: '.claude/CLAUDE.md' }, { relativePath: 'CLAUDE.local.md', logicalName: 'CLAUDE.local.md' }];`. The logicalName stays posix-spelled so the qualified key is stable on Windows (`join` would yield `.claude\CLAUDE.md`) and distinct from plain `CLAUDE.md` — `qualifiedKey` (:250-264) puts logicalName last, so no collision. Then rewrite the loop at :1088-1091 to iterate it: `fileRecord('instruction', join(workingDirectory, entry.relativePath), projectScope, entry.logicalName, '', projectRealRoot)`. Order matters and is already correct this way: `promptLayers.sort((a,b) => a.order - b.order)` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:253) is stable and all four share `scopeSpecificity('project') = 3`, so insertion order decides — `.claude/CLAUDE.md` must sit AFTER `CLAUDE.md` and BEFORE `CLAUDE.local.md` to keep `memory.md:155`'s "`CLAUDE.local.md` is appended after `CLAUDE.md`". Leave :845 (nested), :987 (workspace root) and :1074-1087 (ancestors) on `PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES` — none of the three locations is documented to carry `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and the containment guard `projectRealRoot` already covers the new path via `fileRecord`'s `insideRealRoot` check (:355-356). Roughly four lines plus the constant.

The pre-trust consent report must list the file, or the user approves a project whose instruction content the dialog never named. A naive add is SILENTLY DROPPED: `boundNames` (:85-90) filters through `isSafeName` (:67-72), which rejects any name containing `/`. So add a separate item rather than a new entry in `detectInstructions`: after :205, `const claudeDirInstructions = makeItem('AGENTS_MD', '.claude/CLAUDE.md', existsSync(join(root, '.claude', 'CLAUDE.md')) && insideRealRoot(join(root, '.claude', 'CLAUDE.md'), realRoot) ? ['CLAUDE.md'] : []); if (claudeDirInstructions) items.push(claudeDirInstructions);`. `sourceLabel` is a free-form string already carrying values like `.claude/agents` (:215) and `.claude/settings.json` (:224), so no protocol or i18n change. `ITEM_TYPE_ORDER` (:36-44) already holds `AGENTS_MD`; the sort at :228 is by itemType only, so the two AGENTS_MD rows keep insertion order.

change.symbol: describe 'buildNativeCapabilityInventory — instruction files up to the project root' (:370)
change.what: Two cases. Positive: a trusted cwd holding ONLY `.claude/CLAUDE.md` yields exactly one project-scope instruction record with `logicalName === '.claude/CLAUDE.md'` and `sourcePath === join(cwd, '.claude', 'CLAUDE.md')` (today it yields zero — this is the failing test that proves the gap). Negative/boundary, to pin the deliberate narrowness: a STRICT ANCESTOR's `.claude/CLAUDE.md` produces no record (memory.md:153), and with both `<cwd>/CLAUDE.md` and `<cwd>/.claude/CLAUDE.md` present both records exist with the `.claude` one ordered after plain `CLAUDE.md` and before `CLAUDE.local.md`.

One case: a root holding only `.claude/CLAUDE.md` produces an `AGENTS_MD` item with `sourceLabel: '.claude/CLAUDE.md'` and `names: ['CLAUDE.md']`. Guards the `isSafeName` trap above — without it a silent drop looks like a passing change.

Adjacent, comment-or-code: the comment asserts `--add-dir` loads `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/*.md` and `CLAUDE.local.md`, but the implementation behind `NESSY_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_MEMORY` (native-sources.ts:930-939) loads only `<root>/.claude/rules` and `<root>/.agents/rules`. Either implement the instruction half for add-dir roots or correct the comment; the same sentence is copied into packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/rules-scope-gating.test.ts:10. Not required by this page — file it as its own row rather than smuggling it in.

blastRadius: Adding one record changes the capability GENERATION hash, so it invalidates the pinned-block cache and every downstream projection of it — this crosses the prompt/wire boundary and is a risk trigger. Readers, in order: `nativeRuntimeBinding` case 'instruction' -> `RuntimePromptLayer` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:966-967) and its generation material at :2374-2379; `buildAgentRuntimeView` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:215-216, sort at :253); `composePinnedCapabilityContext` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:960-975), which emits ONE MORE `InstructionsLoaded` hook event per session with `load_reason: 'session_start'` (:1043-1046) — an observable hook payload change for any plugin listening; the nested lazy channel's dedupe (`alreadyLoaded` built from `eagerInstructionFiles.file_path`, base-agent.ts:1248-1251), which means the newly-eager file is automatically suppressed on the lazy path — no double delivery, but any test asserting today's lazy delivery of `<cwd>/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/nested-instruction-discovery.test.ts, packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/nested-instruction-traversal.test.ts) will flip; the Pi subprocess IPC surface — `materializePiContextResources` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/context-resource.ts:63-65) mints a descriptor id from `idPart(key)` which sanitizes `/` to `_` (:24-26), and the harness manifest folds promptLayers into its hash (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:368) — so the Pi manifest changes and forces a re-projection; the `/context` breakdown's Memory-files row (packages/pi-agent-server/src/context-categories.ts:149-154, name derived from the layer key). The consent change crosses the RPC to the renderer trust dialog: `ProjectContributionReport` in packages/shared/src/protocol/capabilities.ts — payload content only, no schema change. `claudeMdExcludes` still applies (the post-pass filter at native-sources.ts:1131-1133 matches absolute `sourcePath`). No persistence boundary: instruction records are derived per generation, nothing is written to disk.
userImpact: A user opens a trusted repo that keeps its instructions at `.claude/CLAUDE.md` — Claude Code's documented alternative, and the layout repos use when they keep all tooling config under `.claude/`. On the default Pi runtime the model receives NO project instructions: it ignores the repo's build/test commands and conventions exactly as if the file did not exist, `/context` -> Memory files does not list it, and the pre-trust 'what this project contributes' dialog shows no project-instructions row, so nothing tells the user the file was skipped. It is worse than plain absence in one way: if the agent later happens to read any file under `<cwd>/.claude/` (a settings file, a rule, an agent definition), the nested channel injects the file mid-session, so the same session silently changes behaviour partway through and loses it again at the next compaction. The same repo behaves differently across backends in the same app — on the opt-in Claude provider the Agent SDK loads the file itself (claude-agent.ts:305), so a user comparing the two backends sees the project's conventions honoured on one and not the other.

The doc page was re-fetched with `curl -sL` (477 lines) and `memory.md` likewise; quotes are from the raw Markdown, not a summary. Two things I could NOT settle from the docs. (1) The pages say 'either/or' and never state what happens when BOTH `./CLAUDE.md` and `./.claude/CLAUDE.md` exist — prefer-one vs load-both is unspecified. The change above loads both, which follows `memory.md:155` ('All discovered files are concatenated into context rather than overriding each other') and is the fail-open choice; if a later measurement of real Claude Code shows preference, the loop needs a first-match break at that tier only. (2) Whether Claude also accepts `.claude/CLAUDE.local.md` — no page says so, so the change deliberately does not add it. The `settingSources`-gating half of the same doc sentence (divergence (c)) is real in code but has no production producer, so it cannot be observed today; it is listed as adjacent rather than folded into this fix.
